idiom_name: absent or unit value, default instance, or a minimal do-nothing stand-in
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: pass the runtime's absent value where the type allows it (null, nil, None, undefined, nullptr), the unit value where the language has one ((), std::monostate, akka.NotUsed), a default-constructed instance where a value is mandatory, or - as the last resort - a minimal implementation whose members do nothing. There is no configuration, no expectation and no behaviour: the placeholder exists only to satisfy the signature, and the validity of the test rests on the exercised path never reading it. Where the parameter demands a full interface, that do-nothing implementation is hand-written, which is why the language-neutral baseline is manual; make it fail loudly (throw, panic, assert) when the point is to pin the assumption, and keep it inert when the point is merely to satisfy the signature.
code_sketch:
session = Session(config, clock=absent, sink=absent)   # placeholders, never read
run_path(session)              # exercises and asserts the behaviour under test

# where the type demands a value, take the cheapest one the runtime offers:
placeholder = Default.new_instance_of(Collaborator)     # or a do-nothing implementation
pitfalls: Documenting the assumption nowhere: a placeholder without a name or comment saying 'unused on this path' turns the next path change into a mystery failure.
Fabricating behaviour on the placeholder (canned answers, recorded calls) - that is a stub or a spy and belongs to a different pattern.
Reusing one placeholder instance through a shared fixture, so a path that starts reading it mutates state visible to other tests.

Typed nil interfaces in Go: an interface variable holding a nil concrete pointer is not 'nil' at the type level — passing it where the SUT does a nil-check returns false and the SUT may try to use it, causing a panic instead of the expected silent pass-through. Use an explicit no-op struct implementation (DiscardNotifier, NoopLogger) rather than a raw nil interface.

Silent dummies masking newly read parameters: a Dummy that returns zero values, empty strings, or default-constructed objects lets the test pass with fabricated data when a parameter that was previously unused starts being read — the failure surfaces not in the test but as a downstream wrong-answer bug.

Shared mutable dummy state across tests: a module-level dummy struct with mutable fields (a counter, a slice, a delegate) reused across tests causes cross-test contamination — the state observed by test B depends on what test A did to the shared instance.

Parameter-as-code-smell left unaddressed: a parameter that every path ignores is not a testing problem — it is a design problem. Paying for a placeholder in every test indefinitely defers the real fix: remove the parameter, make it optional, or model its absence explicitly in the production signature.

Swift Optional unwrapping silently succeeds with nil: code that uses if-let or guard-let on a dummy Optional will silently skip the branch when the parameter is read, making the exercised path appear to work correctly while the dependency is silently ignored — the real branch is never tested.

Wrong move: use a lenient Mockito mock as the dummy because 'it is never called' -> unstubbed methods silently return null, 0, false or empty collections, so the day the exercised path starts reading the parameter the test stays green on fabricated defaults -> instead enable STRICT_STUBS (or spec the mock against the real interface) so an unintended interaction fails at once.

Wrong move: use Unit (Scala) or BoxedUnit (Java) as the no-value placeholder in a generic signature -> void/Unit leaks across Scala/Java interop and forces cross-language signature hacks, which is exactly what Akka's 2.4 migration away from them fixed -> instead use a dedicated placeholder type like akka.NotUsed designed to mean 'no value here' in both languages.

Wrong move: default-construct a std::variant whose first alternative has no default constructor -> the variant is not default-constructible and the code fails to compile or ends up in valueless_by_exception -> instead list std::monostate as the first alternative so 'no value' is an explicit, queryable state rather than an accident.
